Let’s break this down step by step.  

1. The expression is:  
   \( ( \text{not False} ) \ \text{or} \ ( \text{False} ) \)  

2. Evaluate \( \text{not False} \):  
   \( \text{not False} = \text{True} \)  

3. Now the expression becomes:  
   \( \text{True} \ \text{or} \ \text{False} \)  

4. In Boolean logic, \( \text{True} \ \text{or} \ \text{False} \) evaluates to \( \text{True} \).  

Final answer: true
